title: Monroe and Texas territory, Hot Springs nightclub job
summary: Hamilton recalls musicians he met around Monroe, the touring show bands that wintered there, and four months at a Hot Springs nightclub.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Texas, that was our territory. We done good. Well, I had a chance to meet a lot of guys and get a lot of experience in music, along in that line. And a lot of the musicians I met and sang, a lot of boys from Alexander, John Duncan, Zeb, and Tav Krohn, a lot of the fellas around there. And there was a bunch of fellas there now from Elorade around there, Leonard Parker, and there was a fine little excellent banjo player around there, and we called him Baby Buster. And he was a guy, he picked a lot of solos, and he was fast. And there was some boys who used to come there in winter after the show, the Rabbit Foot Show and the Silas Green Show. The musicians, most of them, would winter in Monroe, and I had a chance to meet all those guys, and I learned a lot of things from those guys they showed me. So I left after the band, Harry Walker took the band over, and I went on to Hot Springs. I went over there and played over there at a nightclub over there with another bunch of fellas around there, at Wilson's Place down on Melvin Avenue. And I stayed over there about four months in Hot Springs. We played, they were rocking. Well, his nightclub was in, it was a seasonable place, and certain seasons when the tourists would be there, you'd have a nightclub down there. So I played down there about three months, and well after the season closed I went back to Monroe.
